source_text: hominem Deus non fecerit, aut diabolo fecerit, aut diabolus fecerit Peccatorum quoque genitalibus manum divinae providentiae interesse ex eadem concupiscentiae voluptate concretum etiam Isaac
pass_a_gloss: Human-being God not fecerit, or to-the-devil fecerit, or the-devil fecerit of-sins also genitalibus manum divinae providentiae interesse from the-same of-desire by-pleasure concretum also Isaac.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Married people conceived without bodily warmth.
God did not make the human being; or he made the human being for the devil; or the devil made the human being.
Isaac too was formed from that same pleasure of sexual desire.
The hand of divine providence is at work even in the sexual organs of sinners.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
